clue.text: Sheep gatherer gets right on the vessel

parts.note: a collie is the classic sheepdog that rounds up a flock

explanation.surface: A shepherd's dog gets the right to come aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets ... on the' are link words: R is put on the end of COLLIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a ship built to carry coal.

clue.text: Expired with a frog in the throat?

definitions.text: with a frog in the throat?
definitions.meaning: speaking hoarsely, as a frog calls

explanation.definitionFit: A slang verb for dying, and also uttering a hoarse frog-like call.

clue.text: Contributory factor to rustiness

parts.note: not corrosion of metal but skills that fade when not used regularly

explanation.surface: Something that helps metal corrode.
explanation.walkthrough: Rustiness here is lost skill, not oxidised iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Not keeping skills in use leaves a performer out of shape.

clue.text: Holly covering one Latin law

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: Holly wrapped around an ancient legal statute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is a link word here: I sits above LEX in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus name for the holly family, also used for the holm oak.

clue.text: Foreign tongue used at one time in sorrow

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: rue is regret or sorrow
then means at that time in the past

explanation.surface: A foreign language once spoken in grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a link word. Ruthene is an old name for the Ruthenian language of the Carpathians.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the Ruthenians, an East Slavic people of central Europe.

clue.text: Nursery slope climber

parts.note: not a beginner skier but a figure from a nursery rhyme who went up a hill with her brother to fetch water

explanation.surface: A novice skier tackling the gentle beginners' run.
explanation.walkthrough: A nursery slope is a beginners' ski run, but here 'Nursery' means nursery rhyme: Jack and Jill went up the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme, the girl climbs the hill with Jack to fetch a pail of water.

clue.text: Diminutive Jane in Spain

parts.note: the Spanish form of the girl's name with its affectionate little ending

explanation.surface: A petite woman called Jane on holiday in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' looks like small in stature but means a pet form of a name: Juana with the Spanish ending -ita.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish girl's name, the affectionate little form of Juana.

clue.text: Capital distribution of mail

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Delivering the post across the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Search extensively in the diocese for Sir Harry…

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Hunting all over the bishop's territory for a knight named Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. Sir Harry Secombe was a Welsh comedian and singer, one of the Goons on BBC radio.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh entertainer, knighted, best known from The Goon Show.

clue.text: … taking the shortest route

parts.note: travelling in a straight line, like a bird heading directly home

explanation.surface: Going the most direct way.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 7 down for the surface only; the definition stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a straight-line distance, ignoring roads and bends.

clue.text: Soothing to some, but Leo's rustic charm is shattered by it

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Some find it calming, but it wrecks the rural appeal for Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is shattered' rearranges the fifteen letters of LEOS RUSTIC CHARM; 'but' and 'by it' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Symphonies and other works for a full ensemble of players are what some listeners find calming.

clue.text: Ken sounds negative

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for negative is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: no is the negative reply

explanation.surface: A man called Ken comes across as a pessimist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a man's name but is the Scottish verb meaning to be aware of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ken is to be acquainted with or understand, a Scots verb for having knowledge.

clue.text: Cross-line that backfires

parts.note: the word for shoots read back to front gives the little stroke across the end of a printed letter

explanation.surface: A crossing cable or rope that recoils dangerously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfires' splits as 'back' plus 'fires': FIRES written backwards gives the typographical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A typographic finishing stroke crossing the end of a letter's main stem.

clue.text: Bordering on a cough

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a hem is the border of cloth, and to hem is to border

explanation.surface: Almost coughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordering on' looks like 'almost', but splits: HEM (border) put on A.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate throat-clearing noise made to attract attention.

clue.text: Steamed up as a seaman over fuel

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: AB, able-bodied, is a rating of seaman
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Getting angry like a sailor over petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling, said of liquid seething with bubbles and heat.

clue.text: Bet by post

definitions.meaning: a pointed wooden pole driven into the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The same word means a wager and a sharpened pole or stick.

clue.text: Number getting up can be open to trickery

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
someone getting up is up, out of bed
able means one can, so able to be

explanation.surface: A digit rising might leave one vulnerable to deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a common way for 'number' to give one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easily deceived or gulled is a natural victim of a swindle.

clue.text: An item covered in paper

definitions.meaning: a single thing among a set of goods
a piece of writing reported in a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A thing for sale and a newspaper report share the one word for a separate piece.

clue.text: Father extremely supple albeit infirm

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
very lithe and nimble

explanation.surface: Dad is remarkably flexible though in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'albeit' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak and delicate in health, easily broken.

clue.text: Purchasing point one thinks of mechanically

definitions.text: Purchasing point one thinks of mechanically

parts.words: Purchasing point one thinks of mechanically
parts.note: purchase here is grip or leverage, and the point is where a lever pivots

explanation.surface: A shop counter that some people treat in a robotic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' in mechanics means leverage, so the purchasing point is where a lever turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The pivot or support on which a lever turns.

clue.text: Source of an asthmatic remedy peer had made up

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nobleman concocted a cure for wheezing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub yielding the alkaloid ephedrine, used to ease bronchial breathing.

clue.text: Perks for the croupier at work?

definitions.text: Perks for the croupier at work?

parts.words: Perks for the croupier at work?
parts.note: a croupier at a casino table pulls chips away with a stick, and a cut of the takings is a perk

explanation.surface: What a casino dealer gets as fringe benefits on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The croupier literally draws chips in with a rake, while the phrase also means a share of profits, often an illicit one.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission or cut, often dishonest, taken from a sum of money.

clue.text: Attained by Marxist suffering inside

indicators.note: inside puts one piece within the other

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Achieved by a communist in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrived at or achieved a goal.

clue.text: Volunteers may have good cause to tire towards the end of it

definitions.text: Volunteers may have good cause to tire towards the end of it

parts.words: Volunteers may have good cause to tire towards the end of it
parts.note: charity collectors weary by evening of the day they rattle tins for a good cause, and to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: Charity helpers are naturally exhausted late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: A flag day was a British street collection day when donors got a small paper flag; 'flag' also means tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of street collecting for a charity, givers receiving a paper badge.

clue.text: European given leave on time

parts.note: to leave something be is to let it

explanation.surface: A continental traveller is allowed to depart promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Latvia in northern Europe.

clue.text: Young hog is quiet with cereal

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
oats are a grain crop

explanation.surface: A piglet stays silent while eating its grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A weaned piglet, a word used chiefly in North America.

clue.text: Old king is tender, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for tender is only heard aloud

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch is gentle, so rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like gentle but is the verb, to put forward. Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, of Offa's Dyke fame.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Saxon ruler of Mercia in the eighth century.

clue.text: Comforting substance in a herbal mixture

indicators.note: in signals letters sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A soothing ointment made from a blend of herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing ointment or healing salve.

clue.text: Leading actor of performing arts

indicators.note: letters performing a routine move about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A headline player from the world of theatre and music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal performer who heads a cast.

clue.text: The highest-ever bidder in bloodstock records!

definitions.text: The highest-ever bidder in bloodstock records!

parts.words: The highest-ever bidder in bloodstock records!
parts.note: the Shakespeare monarch who cried that he would give his kingdom for a horse

explanation.surface: A record-breaking buyer at a racehorse auction.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play the king at Bosworth offers 'My kingdom for a horse!', a bid no bloodstock sale could beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenet monarch whose famous line offers a whole realm for one mount.

clue.text: She gets the pip in the after noon

definitions.text: She gets the pip in the after noon

parts.words: She gets the pip in the after noon
parts.note: in old signalling alphabets P was pip and M was a woman's name, so afternoon, PM, was pip followed by her

explanation.surface: A woman becomes irritated each afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'get the pip' is British slang for being annoyed. In the old army signals alphabet PM was 'pip emma', so the woman follows pip after noon.
explanation.definitionFit: The signallers' code name for the letter M, a woman's name, partnered pip in the time after midday.

clue.text: Ready as can be, I suppose

indicators.note: what the letters can be when rearranged signals an anagram here

explanation.surface: As prepared as possible, I imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges READY AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedging phrase meaning I venture or presume, used when conceding a point.
